content:
There are many reasons to not do that. One is for example aggregates are propagated before they are validated. If the aggregates are from different slots the balances are kinda empty because they could have been already included: say for example there's a fork in slots 2, 3 and now slot 4 is missed, some of the attestations from slot 2 got included in 3 and now you see aggregates for those attestations again, do you count them or not? you can't even know this on gossip. 

If you are forked you want to include attestations from all branches, this will include from only one of them (typically aggregators are peered to one of the branches), etc.

author: jtraglia
content:
> Gossip now handles aggregates differently depending on whether their
> slot has ended. During its slot, none of an aggregate's attestations can
> be on chain yet, since attestations are first included in the next
> slot, so an aggregate is only forwarded if it has more attesting
> balance than the best one seen for the same data and committee. This
> cuts most of the redundant traffic from a committee's aggregators. Once
> the slot has ended, some of its attestations may already be included on
> one fork but not another, so attesting balance no longer shows how much
> an aggregate adds and could be inflated with attestations that are
> already on chain. A late aggregate is instead only ignored if an
> aggregate already seen covers all of its attesters, which never drops a
> vote.
